claims.text: Wear resistance will improve as ambient temperature rises from 25 °C to approximately 600–700 °C.
The intermediate-temperature improvement in wear resistance is caused by activation of dynamic recrystallization and self-healing.
Wear performance will degrade sharply above approximately 700 °C.
High-temperature degradation is caused by diffusion-driven phase instability and loss of solid-solution strengthening.
An as-deposited CoCrFeMnNi or W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf-based HEA coating on a transition-metal matrix has a fine-grained, high-dislocation-density microstructure.
Nano-precipitates or interstitial O and C stabilize the initial coating matrix.
Strain rates of 10^-3 to 10^-1 s^-1 are typical equivalents for tribological contact.
Dynamic recrystallization is active in the coating at intermediate temperatures of 500–700 °C.
M23C6 or Mn2O3 precipitates and interstitial O or C impede dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding.
Diffusion of Si or O at 500–700 °C seals surface cracks or reforms protective oxide layers.
Crack sealing and protective-oxide reformation reduce wear at intermediate temperatures.
Above the critical temperature, lattice diffusion and precipitate coarsening cause a loss of Orowan strengthening.
High-temperature grain growth, softening, and breakdown of the protective surface layer cause a sharp increase in wear rate.
The specific wear rate will decrease from 25 °C to about 650 °C and then increase sharply above about 700 °C.
The wear-rate reversal coincides with a transition from slip or twinning to full dynamic recrystallization and precipitate dissolution.
Room-temperature wear resistance of the as-deposited coating is dominated by high dislocation density and nano-precipitate strengthening.
The degradation boundary is between 700 °C and 800 °C for CoCrFeMnNi-based systems.
HEA systems containing lower-melting-point constituents may have a lower degradation boundary.
Composition and interstitial O or C content can shift phase-stability and recrystallization temperatures.
The effect of thermal-expansion mismatch between the coating and transition-metal substrate is not quantified by the cited evidence.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says dynamic recrystallization is activated and beneficial at 500–700 °C, whereas the boundary defines 700–800 °C as the point at which the activation energy for dynamic recrystallization is exceeded. These statements assign inconsistent activation ranges to DRX.

Dynamic recrystallization is initially presented as the cause of improved wear resistance, but full dynamic recrystallization is later said to coincide with the wear-rate reversal and degradation without clearly explaining why its effect changes sign.
